transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

Since I stopped working full-time, I keep starting projects for the museum and then just never finishing them, even when I really want to. Ever since I retired from my handyman job a couple of years ago, I just can't seem to follow through on these volunteer tasks, and I'm honestly starting to worry it might be a sign of early cognitive decline.

Do you find that you're still interested in these museum projects when you start them, but something gets in the way of completing them, or has your interest in activities decreased overall since your retirement?

Oh, my interest hasn't decreased at all; I'm actually very excited about these projects and really want to do them. The trouble is that I get easily sidetracked by other things, like sorting through my old photos or reading about a new exhibit, and I just struggle to follow through to the end.
Do you find that you're having trouble sitting still or feeling restless, like you need to be constantly doing something, even when you're not working on a project?
No, I don't really feel physically restless or have trouble sitting still. It's more that my mind tends to wander and I lose my focus, rather than needing to constantly move around.
Have you been feeling sad, empty, or hopeless since your retirement, or has your mood been generally stable?
No, I haven't really felt sad, empty, or hopeless. I'm just quite frustrated and worried about my focus and memory since retiring. Aside from that, my mood has been pretty stable.

Can you tell me more about what happens when you try to focus on one of these museum projects - do you feel like you're intentionally choosing to switch to something else, or does your attention just seem to drift away without you realizing it?

It is definitely not an intentional choice; my attention just drifts away without me even realizing it. For instance, I’ll be sitting in a planning meeting and suddenly "snap back" only to realize I missed a big chunk of what was being discussed. Other times, I'll start setting up a workshop and end up sidetracked sorting old photos, only realizing much later that the original task was left completely unfinished.

Do you think if someone was working alongside you on these projects, helping to keep you on track, you would be able to complete them, or do you feel like there's something inherent in the way you're approaching tasks that's causing you to not follow through?

I'm not quite sure, to be honest. I've always tried to handle all of these organizing tasks on my own, so I haven't really thought about whether having someone work alongside me would keep my mind from drifting off.
Have you experienced difficulties with organization, time management, or self-regulation of emotions throughout your life, not just since your retirement?

Yes, these issues actually go all the way back to my childhood. Even in elementary school, my teachers would tell my parents that I was bright but constantly daydreaming, losing track of instructions, and forgetting to hand in homework I had actually completed.
Have you ever acted on impulse, doing things without much thought, like interrupting others, blurting out answers, or engaging in impulsive behaviors, throughout your life?

I don't really recall having issues with impulsivity, blurting things out, or interrupting people. My struggles have always been much more about losing focus, daydreaming, and getting sidetracked rather than acting impulsively.

Have you experienced significant difficulties with sustaining attention in tasks or play activities throughout your life, such as making careless mistakes or failing to finish tasks, that are not solely explained by your reported daydreaming?

Yes, my difficulty with following through on tasks goes way beyond just daydreaming and has been a lifelong issue. Even as a child in school, I would lose track of instructions and forget to hand in homework I had actually completed. Now, that same pattern makes me start setting up museum workshops only to get sidetracked and leave them half-done.

Have you ever been diagnosed with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) or experienced symptoms of inattention, such as difficulty sustaining focus during tasks, that have caused significant impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning throughout your life?

I have never been formally diagnosed with ADHD, which is why I wanted to get this assessment. I've definitely struggled with inattention my whole life, starting with schoolteachers calling me a daydreamer, and now it's causing real issues with my volunteering, like double-booking rooms and missing deadlines.
Have you ever experienced symptoms of hyperactivity, such as fidgeting, feeling restless, or talking excessively, in addition to your difficulties with attention and focus?

No, I haven't really experienced those physical symptoms of hyperactivity like fidgeting, restlessness, or talking too much. My struggles have always been much more about my mind drifting off and losing focus.
